In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
AD is an important damping mechanism for MRI turbulence in very weakly-ionized gas and the MRI is suppressed by AD in protoplanetary disk midplanes.
the MRI is a robust instability in weakly ionized protoplanetary disks with a saturation level that is reduced but not eliminated by the effect of AD.
the MRI in the strong-coupling limit is suppressed by a factor of 10-100 for Am = 10-1 and a factor of 1000 for Am = 100.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
AD is not a significant effect in the saturated state of MRI turbulence for Am > ~0.1.
the effect of AD on the MRI is to decrease the saturated stress by an order of magnitude or more, and this effect is most pronounced in disks with very weak net magnetic flux.
the MRI turbulence is significantly suppressed when AD is strong (i.e., Am 1) in the strong coupling limit.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the MRI in protoplanetary disk can be very efficient at driving turbulence in the inner regions of the disks, where the magnetic field is weak and the gas is highly ionized by cosmic rays.
the MRI turbulence is suppressed by AD, and the saturated level of α is determined by the competition between the magnetic tension force and AD.
AD suppresses MRI turbulence and limits the stress in the disk, and thus it is important to include AD in models of the MRI in very weakly magnetized disks.
